title: Phase 4 Signal Pipeline: strength-weighted consolidation + per-strategy risk budgets + actual win_rate sizing
description: Upgrade the signal pipeline to use win-rate-aware decision making: (1) replace net-vote consolidation in SignalGenerator.consolidate_signals() with strength-weighted voting where weight = signal.strength * strategy_hit_rates.get(strategy_id, 0.5), (2) add per-strategy risk budget allocation to RiskEngine proportional to strategy win_rate, (3) populate PositionSizer.size() with per-strategy actual win_rate instead of hardcoded 0.5 default.
action: In generator.py:54-69, change consolidate_signals() to accept strategy_hit_rates: dict[str, float] | None = None param. Replace net vote `sum(s.direction.value for s in signals)` with `sum(s.direction.value * s.strength * strategy_hit_rates.get(s.strategy_id, 0.5) for s in signals)`. Replace avg_strength with weighted avg. In risk_engine.py, add strategy_risk_budgets: dict[str, float] param to __init__ and _check_strategy_budget() method that caps per-strategy exposure proportional to win_rate. In position_sizer.py:39, change `win_rate: float = 0.5` default and add strategy_win_rates: dict[str, float] | None = None param to size(); look up signal.strategy_id in strategy_win_rates dict, falling back to win_rate param.

python -c "from quantflow.signal.position_sizer import PositionSizer; ps=PositionSizer(); print('size sig:', ps.size.__code__.co_varnames[:6])" shows strategy_win_rates in signature

implementation: generator.py: Add `strategy_hit_rates: dict[str, float] | None = None` param to consolidate_signals() after signals param. If strategy_hit_rates is None, use empty dict. Compute weights: `hit_rates = strategy_hit_rates or {}; weights = [s.strength * hit_rates.get(s.strategy_id, 0.5) for s in signals]`. Weighted direction: `net = sum(s.direction.value * w for s, w in zip(signals, weights, strict=True))`. Weighted strength: `total_weight = sum(weights); avg_strength = total_weight / len(signals) if total_weight > 0 else 0.0`

risk_engine.py: Add `strategy_risk_budgets: dict[str, float] | None = None` to __init__. Store as `self._strategy_risk_budgets = strategy_risk_budgets or {}`. Add method: `def _check_strategy_budget(self, signal: Signal, portfolio: Portfolio) -> RiskDecision:` — if signal.strategy_id in self._strategy_risk_budgets, sum position values for that strategy across portfolio, check against total_value * budget_pct. Insert `self._check_strategy_budget` in checks list after `self._check_portfolio_limit`

success_metrics: consolidate_signals with strategy_hit_rates produces direction weighted by strength * hit_rate
PositionSizer.size with strategy_win_rates={'trend': 0.65} produces larger size than default win_rate=0.5
RiskEngine has _check_strategy_budget in its checks pipeline

reference.pattern: Follow existing method signatures and parameter patterns. Use Optional dict params with None default and `or {}` fallback, consistent with existing codebase style.

rationale.chosen_approach: Strength-weighted consolidation ensures that strategies with higher hit rates have proportionally more influence on the final signal direction. Per-strategy risk budgets prevent over-allocation to low win-rate strategies. Actual win_rate in Kelly sizing correctly sizes positions based on observed performance rather than a blanket 0.5 assumption.
decision_factors: Current net-vote gives equal weight to all strategies regardless of quality — a 55% win-rate trend strategy gets same vote as 35% win-rate strategy
Kelly criterion is highly sensitive to win_rate input: 0.5 vs 0.65 produces significantly different optimal f*
strategy_hit_rates dict is optional (None default) so existing callers work without changes
rationale.tradeoffs: Requires callers to provide strategy_win_rates / strategy_hit_rates dicts — adds coupling but corrects a fundamental sizing error

risks: Backward compatibility: strategy_hit_rates/strategy_win_rates are optional with None default, preserving current behavior when not provided
Risk budget check may reject valid signals if budget percentages are too tight — default None means no budget check applied
